title: Rational Number Classification Interactive
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Algebra I
Number Systems and Properties
Rational Number Classification Interactive
description: Students decide whether each of 16 numbers is rational, write the rational ones as p/q, and see why with a number line, a zoomed view, a fraction bar, and step-by-step explanations.

learningObjectives: Classify a number as rational or not rational using the definition p/q with integers p and q, q not 0.
Express integers, terminating decimals, repeating decimals, and mixed numbers in the form p/q.
Explain why terminating and repeating decimals are rational and why non-repeating, non-terminating decimals are not.
Distinguish a rational approximation such as 22/7 from the irrational number it approximates.
prerequisites: Converting a terminating decimal to a fraction
The definition of a rational number

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification practice with immediate feedback, a fraction-writing follow-up, and step-through explanations
keyQuestions: Can this number be written as p/q with integers p and q, q not 0?
Does the decimal end, repeat, or do neither?
How can a repeating decimal be turned into a fraction?
commonMisconceptions: A decimal that goes on forever is never rational
A decimal with a visible pattern must be rational
assessmentOpportunities: Students explain why the square root of 9 is rational and the square root of 2 is not
